method_family: Explainable Boosting Machine (GA2M with pairwise interactions) on concatenated FreeSurfer MRI volumes/thicknesses, cognitive scores and demographic/APOE4 features (feature-level fusion), with SMOTE and 5-fold CV
what_it_shows: The study runs three matched EBM arms at 1-5 year horizons: Comb (a), MRI + cognitive scores; Comb (b), cognitive scores only; Comb (c), MRI only. All three arms also carry age, gender, education, baseline diagnosis (EMCI/LMCI) and APOE4. The authors report that Comb (a) had the highest AUC at every horizon ('significantly higher'; Fig. 2d). The 5-year Comb (a) AUC is about 0.92 with accuracy 85%. The magnitudes are figure-only.
why: PDF identity: the title, authors (Cai, Hu, Ma, Si, Chen, Gong, Zhang, Yan, Chen; Xi'an Jiaotong University), Brain Sci 2023 13:1535 and the DOI match the P-211 block (header = filename). Block defect: the block's sample-size field reads '242804 - META-ANALYSIS: 66 articles, 242,804 community dwellers'. That is wrong: the PDF states 1042 amnestic MCI, and the registry Sample_N_Approx (242804) carries the same error; both need repair. The comparison is a within-study head-to-head of the fused feature set against each single-modality feature set, with the same auxiliary covariates in every arm. Comb (a) vs Comb (c) isolates the effect of adding cognitive scores to an MRI model, which fits the narrowed wording ('... or cognitive scores'). Comb (a) vs Comb (b) and Comb (c) tests fusion against the best single-modality baseline, which fits the stated form. Round 20 treated generic fusion as in scope and failed P-81 only because fusion did not beat the best unimodal baseline; on that reading P-211 passes on AUC. Caveats the reviewer should weigh: (1) The magnitudes are figure-only. My approximate reading of Fig. 2d gives Comb (a)/(c)/(b) AUC of about 0.90/0.89/0.78 at 1 year, 0.80/0.77/0.70 at 2 years, 0.75/0.70/0.745 at 3 years, 0.87/0.85/0.82 at 4 years and 0.92/0.905/0.85 at 5 years. The gain over MRI-only is therefore small at 1 and 5 years (about 0.01-0.015) and within the SD error bars, and at 3 years Comb (a) and Comb (b) nearly tie. (2) 'Significantly higher' is asserted, but no significance test is described. (3) On accuracy, Comb (a) is not clearly above Comb (c) at 1, 4 and 5 years (figure). In the long term Comb (b) has the highest specificity and Comb (c) the highest sensitivity, which the authors state themselves. (4) There is circularity: CDR-SB, FAQ, MMSE and ADAS13 are features while the outcome is clinical AD diagnosis, the same issue noted for P-81. (5) Validation is internal only (90/10 split, SMOTE, 5-fold CV). (6) The fusion is generic feature concatenation in a GAM, not a dedicated auxiliary-data-aware architecture. If the reviewer reads 'auxiliary-data-aware fusion' as an architecture class rather than as 'fusion with auxiliary data', the stated verdict drops to partly. Independence: the data are ADNI, the same dataset family as all three current supporters and as P-1. The method family (a boosted GAM on concatenated tabular features) differs from P-3 (3D CNN attention transfer), P-104 (sparse regression + SVM with side-information) and P-81 (CNN late fusion). No shared authors with the supporters (Luo et al.; Shen, Zhu et al.; Cao, Ma, Nayak, Duong). Peer-reviewed MDPI journal article, not a preprint. Figure values were read from a PyMuPDF render of p.7 saved at out/VF-15/img/P-211_p7.png.

quotes.quote: In each follow-up period, we trained three EBM classifiers based on the following three feature combinations: ... Comb. (a) both MRI-driven biomarkers and cognitive test scores, plus age, gender, education, diagnose at baseline, and APOE4.
Comb. (b) Cognitive test scores, plus age, gender, education, diagnose at baseline, and APOE4. Comb. (c) MRI-driven biomarkers, plus age, gender, education, diagnose at baseline, and APOE4.

As shown in Figure 2, the classification AUC value derived from the joint use of Comb (a) were found to be significantly higher than those of other feature combinations. The mean AUC using Comb (a) displayed a characteristic pattern of first at about 0.9, then decreasing, reaching a low point at 3 years, followed by a gradual increase until 5 years of follow-up, to about 0.92.
According to the AUC value, the Comb (a) outperformed the other feature combinations’ performances in all periods (Figure 2d).
In the long-term follow-up period, the specificity of Comb (b) exceeded that of using Comb (a) and Comb (c), while the sensitivity of using Comb (c) exceeded that of the others.

we revealed that incorporating demographic and cognitive measurements into MRI results could slightly improve the prediction performance for future one-year prediction. The improvement was more significant for other future time periods.
The baseline information was used as input of all EBMs and the converting AD or not during follow-up period was used as output. All EBMs were tested with the 5-fold cross validation.
The samples involved in this study was consisted of 1042 Amnestic MCI individuals at baseline from ADNI1, ADNI2, ADNI3, and ADNIGO, which are different phases of ADNI program.
